title: PRD — Deterministic Output Guarantees & Cost-Slicing for Hosted Endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) — Acceptance & Cutover Runbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Objective: Define deterministic output guarantees and a cost-slicing acceptance envelope for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Deliverables: (1) concise behavioral contract for determinism and reproducibility across model variants, quantization profiles, and runtime caching; (2) cost-slicing bands (Quality Tiers) with associated latency/cost SLOs and automated routing policies; (3) end-to-end launch/cutover runbook with testing, canary phases, rollback triggers, and post-launch monitoring dashlets. Motivation: Customers require predictable outputs for regression-sensitive flows (e.g., document summarization, legal drafting, reranking in retrieval systems) and predictable unit economics. Current gap: hosted endpoints can vary slightly across kernel selections, quantization modes, and caching behavior leading to small but material output differences for eval suites. This PRD codifies tolerances, test harnesses, and a staged launch plan to mitigate regressions while unlocking quantized/cost-optimized runtime variants.
scope_changes: Initial scope included only chat/completions — expanded to include embeddings and rerank after stakeholder request (PM sync 2026-02-22)
Removed deep model-editing rollback (deferred to ENG-60812) — cutover relies on model variant fallback instead
Added requirement to validate determinism across Dedicated and Private deployments (non-hosted test matrix)
Limited initial cost-slicing to three Quality Tiers (Q1/Q2/Q3) — plan to add dynamic microbands in next cycle
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral contract: For canonical prompt set (PRD-canon-001), generation endpoints must meet token-level deterministic delta <= 0.5% across kernel/quantization variants when deterministic flag is enabled
Deterministic mode flag (deterministic=true) must be honored end-to-end including KV cache hit paths and prefix-cache warmups
Latency SLOs per Quality Tier: Completions p95 < 250ms (Q1), < 350ms (Q2), < 600ms (Q3)
Embedding p50 < 60ms (Q1) and p95 < 200ms (Q2/Q3), batch-aware throughput documented
Rerank throughput: sustain >= 400 QPS on dedicated canary config for 30m without error rate > 0.5%
Cost per 1k tokens lower bound targets documented and validated for quantized variants (within +/-10% of forecast)
End-to-end evals: regression suite (evals/repro-suite) passes with no regressions labeled 'critical' for the canonical prompt set
Canary rollouts gated by automated checks (see launch_checklist) and manual sign-off from PM, ENG SRE, and Product Security
Operational contracts: incident runbook created, alert thresholds in telemetry dashboard, and retrospective template prepared
Documentation: Console UI shows Quality Tier selection and cost/latency trade-off tooltip; API surface documents deterministic flag behavior
testing_plan: Unit & integration: deterministic flag unit tests for sampling RNG, attention caching, and model variant mapping (ENG PRs linked below)
Repro harness: run repro-suite (canonical prompts x 6 seeds) across kernels: fp16, int8, int8+kv-opt and compare BLEU/EM/METRIC deltas
Load tests: staged 1k/5k/20k qps profiles for rerank and embeddings, observe latency/cost curves and error rates
Chaos tests: simulate KV cache cold-start, network packet loss, and model shard eviction during canary windows
Customer-sim scenarios: run 5 customer-provided prompt sets in sandbox (with NDA) and confirm stability and determinism margins
A/B quality validation: run baseline vs quantized variant on held-out evals and produce human-eval spot checks for borderline cases
launch_checklist: Pre-cutover: final acceptance run with night-run passing (no critical regressions) — attach results to PRD
Feature flags: ship deterministic=true and Quality Tier selection behind flags; default remains current behavior
Canary phase 1 (internal): route 0.5% internal traffic for 24h — automated checks must pass (latency, error rate, regression diff)
Canary phase 2 (alpha external): route 2% of non-critical production traffic for 48h to customers opted into alpha; collect cost telemetry
Canary phase 3 (gradual rollout): incrementally open Quality Tier routing to 10%/30%/100% over 5 days with daily sign-offs
Dashboards: publish 'Determinism Health' and 'Quality Tier Cost vs Latency' boards in Console and PagerDuty alert subscriptions configured
Docs & SDKs: Update API docs, Node/Python SDK behavior examples, and Console tooltips before public rollout
Support readiness: Support runbook, template responses, and playbook triage channels created and tested
Final sign-off: PM, ENG SRE, Research lead, and Security approve release window
monitoring_playbook: Key metrics: per-endpoint p50/p95 latency, error rate, kv-cache-hit-rate, token-cost-per-request, determinism-delta (eval harness metric)
Alerts: error-rate > 0.5% sustained 5m, p95 breach of SLO by > 30% for 10m, determinism-delta median > 0.5% over 1h
Investigations: tie alert to last deploy, kernel selection log, quantization-profile, and routing policy; capture last 1k requests for repro
Automated mitigations: autoswap routing to fallback model variant on capacity or SLO breach; pause Quality Tier promotion if anomalies persist
Post-incident: populate postmortem template linked in links field and escalate to reliability weekly review if recurrence
rollback_conditions: Critical regressions identified by repro-suite on canonical prompts (any new 'critical' label regression)
Sustained error rate > 1% for 15m or p95 latency > 2x target for 30m
Unexpected customer-reported correctness regressions for high-risk customers (severity P0 incidents)
Cost blowout: actual cost per 1k tokens > 1.5x forecast across a 2h window
If triggered, automated routing to last-good model variant and immediate pause of Quality Tier promotions
